# Tasks Document

Document version: v2

Dependency order: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8 → 9. Task 1 adds the durable hold to the state module with no reader; tasks 2 and 3 teach the driver and the document phase to stop on it, still with no producer; task 4 wires the controller's pause, resume and start guard, task 5 the settle pass, wait answers and restart, task 6 the route and the wire field; tasks 7 and 8 change the frontend; task 9 writes the live-verification line. Each task leaves `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build:dashboard` and every existing vitest and worktree e2e suite green with no asserted value changed. No task touches an agent-rules sensitive path and no task creates a new source module, so the planned verifier spend is the default routing only. Task 9 is a measurement task with no `- Test:` seam (implementer-only).

- [ ] 1. Durable hold and write ownership in the state module

  - File: src/controller/__tests__/pause-request.test.ts
  - Test: src/controller/__tests__/pause-request.test.ts — `writeRun(record, { ownsPauseRequest: true })`
  - Note: the owned set-and-clear case already holds at base (the field passes through): regression guard, not a red test. The red cases are the stale-write keep, the terminal drop, the concurrent pair and `readRunSync`.
  - Note: `src/controller/__tests__/paused-at.test.ts` and `src/controller/__tests__/state.test.ts` are not edited; no value they assert changes.
  - Purpose: One durable hold that a stale driver or controller write cannot drop.
  - _Leverage: src/controller/state.ts (RunRecord at 67-101, writeJsonAtomic at 322-327, the sync read in listRunsSync at 348-365, writeRun at 388-394)_
  - _Requirements: 2.5, 2.7, 3.5, 5.1, NFR Reliability_
  - _Prompt: Task: Per design C1 and Requirement 2 AC 7 and Requirement 5 AC 1, add `RunRecord.pauseRequested` (ISO string), export `OPERATOR_PAUSE = 'operator'`, add the optional trailing `opts?: { ownsPauseRequest?: boolean }` to writeRun, and export `readRunSync(id)`. Serialise writeRun per run id in-process with a promise chain; inside one section read `run.json` and write. Without ownsPauseRequest the written pauseRequested is the on-disk value; with it, the incoming value (set or absent). A `done`, `abandoned` or `error` status writes no pauseRequested whatever the options. The pausedAt rule at 388-394 is unchanged. readRunSync returns undefined for a missing or unparsable file. Write the new vitest file with temp SDD_HOME isolation like paused-at.test.ts | Restrictions: Every existing writeRun call site keeps its meaning with no edit; pauseReason stays a free string; no `v` bump; a rejected write must not stall later writes for that id | Success: A normal write over an on-disk pauseRequested keeps it; an owned write sets it and an owned write without it clears it; a write with a terminal status drops it; a stale normal write and an owned set started together through Promise.all end with the field set; readRunSync returns the written record, undefined for a missing id, and undefined for an unparsable file; paused-at.test.ts and state.test.ts pass unchanged; tsc is clean_

  - Test: src/controller/__tests__/runs.test.ts — `runOnce(deps(fx, { isPauseRequested }), 'run-20261011-000000')`
  - Note: the `deps` helper (104-119) gains no default, so every existing runs.test.ts case runs unheld and no value it asserts changes.
  - Note: the merge-stage-entry stop (design C3 point 4) has no dedicated case: any hold set while the last implementation step runs is caught first by an earlier phase stop point (for example the CI poll's shouldStop, `src/controller/phases/implementation.ts:1339-1340`); the in-flight case asserts only the observable outcome.
  - Purpose: A held run finishes its step, acts on the result, then parks instead of spawning the next step.
  - _Leverage: src/controller/runs.ts (RunDeps at 388-411, save at 532-537, pause at 539-542, runMergeStageStep at 621-768, runOnce at 770-989, handleCloseoutOutcome at 1038-1063, handleImplementationOutcome at 1120-1181, handleRetrospectiveOutcome at 1184-1206)_
  - _Requirements: 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.6, 5.3, 5.4, 7.1_

One helper returns `cancelled`, then `operator`, then `usage-window`, else null, and replaces the three inline shouldStop lambdas at 933, 964 and 982. At the runOnce loop top (804-806), after the cancel check, a held run pauses and returns; when resumingMerge is true the same write sets the merge cursor `{ phase: run.phase ?? 'implementation', stepKind: 'merge', attempt: 1 }`. runMergeStageStep stops a held run after its hasMerged return (624) with that cursor, and in the blocked branch after the cancel guard (696), returning stop. A stopped outcome with reason operator pauses in the three handlers at 1045-1048, 1127-1132 and 1188-1191. Add runs.test.ts cases | Restrictions: Never signal or kill a step; leave the cancelled and usage-window branches as they are; do not touch the document phase call (task 3) or the controller (task 4) | Success: A held running record ends paused with pauseReason operator, no resumeAt, no inFlight, and the stub consumed no step; with a hold that is false on its first read and true after, a document step that classifies usage-limit (the fixture at 348-366) ends paused/operator with no resumeAt; a held record seeded merging with an implementation cursor ends paused/operator with cursor stepKind merge and no `pr merge` gh call; a hold set from the setInFlight dep while the last implementation step runs, with the mergeable PR of the auto test at 574-613, leaves the PR unmerged (no `pr merge` gh call) and the run paused/operator; a run that enters the merge stage unheld, reaches a blocked fix-eligible PR, and is held before the merge-fix round stop (696) ends paused/operator with cursor stepKind merge and runMergeFixRound not spawned (no fix-round step consumed); existing runs.test.ts cases pass unchanged; tsc is clean_

- [ ] 4. Controller pause, resume and the start guard
  - File: src/controller/controller.ts
  - File: src/controller/__tests__/controller.test.ts
  - Test: src/controller/__tests__/controller.test.ts — controller.pause(id)
  - Note: the usage-window and resumeNow tests at 234-295 keep every asserted value; the usage-pause resume path is a regression guard (Requirement 4 AC 5).
  - Purpose: Apply the hold at once where no step can be in flight, keep a held run from starting, and end the hold on Resume.
  - _Leverage: src/controller/controller.ts (active at 75, resumeNow at 207-224, schedule and isStartable at 298-345, runDeps at 438-453, save at 524-529); scripts/stub-claude.mjs delayMs at 17 and 110-111_
  - _Requirements: 1.2, 1.5, 1.7, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.6, 4.1, 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 5.2, 7.5, NFR Performance_
  - _Prompt: Task: Per design C4 (interfaces and scheduler item 1) and C5, add `Controller.pause(runId)`: undefined for no run, null for done/abandoned/error, else the record. An already-held run is returned with no write. Otherwise one owned write sets pauseRequested to now; when the run is not in `this.active` and is queued, paused or merging, the same write applies status paused, pauseReason operator, no resumeAt, no inFlight, plus the merge cursor for merging; else the pause is pending. Then `void this.schedule()`. resumeNow gains a first branch for a held run: applied gives one owned write of status queued with pauseRequested, pauseReason and resumeAt absent; pending gives one owned write clearing only pauseRequested; then schedule. save passes opts to writeRun. isStartable returns false for any held run before its status checks. runDeps wires isPauseRequested through the synchronous run read task 1 exports | Restrictions: pause never awaits a step, a signal or gh (Requirement 1 AC 2); resumeNow never writes rate-limit.json for a held run (Requirement 4 AC 3); an unheld run takes today's resumeNow path | Success: Pause on a queued run applies at once and pump() does not start it; pause on a usage-limit run with a future resumeAt sets reason operator and clears resumeAt; pause during a delayed stub step answers before the step ends, the step's result is acted on, and the run ends paused/operator with no inFlight and no further stub run consumed; pause on a merging run applies with the merge cursor and Resume re-enters the merge stage with no implementation step; an operator-paused run stays paused while a window goes over the threshold and recovers; Resume of an applied pause starts the next step; Resume under a full window leaves it paused/usage-window with rate-limit.json unchanged; Resume of a pending pause clears the field and the run finishes; pause returns undefined, null, and the unchanged record (same updated) for unknown, done and held runs; tsc is clean_

In onWaitChange, a held run becomes status paused, pauseReason operator, no resumeAt, instead of queued; the answer is written as today; an abandon on an error or escalation wait still cancels, and task 1's terminal rule drops the hold. recover needs no code change. ## Scope notes

- Carried items from design: none.
- RE-DECIDED in design (D3) and kept here: task 3 stops the document phase only at a review-round top, not before each step Requirement 2 AC 3 lists.
- Not added: a `docs/controller-design.md` §9 update for the operator pause. Neither the decomposition entry nor the design names it; it is left for the close-out.
- Not tested directly: the merge-stage-entry stop (design C3 point 4). Task 2 explains why no fixture reaches it before an earlier stop point; its code is still in task 2's scope.
- Out of scope, as requirements and design set: the advisor second-opinion step, a pause timer, pausing every run with one click, any change to cancel, discard or `scripts/sdd-self-update.sh`.

## Decisions taken in this document

- D1 — The controller work splits into two tasks with the start guard in the first: options were one task, two tasks with the guard in the second; chosen because an applied pause without the guard is started by the scheduler, so task 4's tests could not pass without it.
- D2 — End-to-end seeds use states the live controller never drives: options were seed any state and stop the controller, seed only safe states; chosen safe states (a held applied pause, a usage-limit pause with a future resume time, a waiting run with no wait record) because the worktree suite runs a real controller and a startable seed would spawn a step.
- D3 — The in-flight-last-step case asserts only the observable outcome (no merge, operator pause), not the merge cursor: options were assert the cursor as the design's testing strategy says, assert only the outcome; chosen the outcome because earlier phase stop points catch the hold first and leave the implementation cursor, which also resumes correctly.
- D4 — The wire field and the pause route share one task: options were put the field with the driver task, put it with the route; chosen the route because its test reads the field through the runs list.
- D5 — Frontend tasks are checked by the dashboard build and the worktree e2e suite: options were add a frontend unit-test setup, use the existing checks; chosen the existing checks because the frontend has no unit-test runner and adding one is out of scope.

## Revision History

- **v1** (2026-10-29) — Initial draft.
  - **Lint pass.** 2 fixed; rejected: none.
- **v2** (2026-10-29) — Round-1 adversarial response (adversarial-analysis-tasks.md, verdict iterate 0/1/1).
  - **R1-1 — Accepted (SHOULD_FIX).** The merge-fix round stop was named in task 2's prompt body but had no Success case and no exemption; an exemption would be false, since no earlier stop point catches a hold set during the pull-request read before that stop. Added a Success case: a run entering the merge stage unheld that reaches a blocked, fix-eligible pull request and is held before the merge-fix round ends paused by the operator with the merge cursor and spawns no merge-fix round (task 2 Success, line 27). The merge-stage-entry exemption stays as is.
  - **R1-2 — Accepted (MINOR).** Task 1's prompt body promised the synchronous run read returns nothing for a missing or unparsable file, but its Success named only the missing id. Widened Success to also assert the unparsable file, matching the body and the design (task 1 Success, line 16).
